units.translation: Let him not be a shield-companion to me.
which could also be said as περισταδόν [standing around], which forms are interchanged in the manuscripts of Homer Il. 13, 551.
Show in a circle, standing near, the covering of the man.
For fear stands by instead of sleep.
From these things, the child does not stand by here.
as if you were standing by
to drag into the middle, to cast forth

For surely you have not cast forth this word to be endured.

Hesychius explains it by παραχρήμα [immediately], εὐθέως [straightway], παραυτίκα [at once]. In other writers it is sometimes written παραυτά [immediately] with an acute accent on the last syllable. Coraes observed that πάραυτα [immediately] is still pronounced by the modern Greeks, in the dissertation prefixed to the Prodromus of the Greek Library p. 50, as pointed out by Hermann.
I would say that he went immediately to the city of Ilium.
with an acute accent on the last syllable. immediately
Nor do the shepherds of ships trust in anchorages at once.
this song, madness, derangement destroying the mind
to be out of one's mind
to be out of one's mind
I am out of my mind with fear of the word.
Thus Porson for παραβασίαν [transgression], which in several copies is written παραιβασίαν [transgression], a form used by Hesiod and others.
For I speak of an ancient transgression, swift to avenge.

which the scholiast explains by παραβεβηκότα [having transgressed]. Thus Hermann for περαιβάδαν [transgressor], which is read in M, in the Florentine copy changed to παρβάταν [transgressor], by Triclinius to παρβάδαν [transgressor], written as if this were a Doric form of the adverb like διαρρύδαν [thoroughly] Ch. 67. Meineke in Philol. vol. 19 p. 225 thought βαρίβαν [heavy] should be written, which is not the subject, but placed in comparison for ὡς βαρίβαν [as heavy], about which one should not think. But the truth is undoubtedly παρβάταν [transgressor], or, what comes closer to the manuscript reading, δέ φαμ᾽ ὑπερβάταν [but I say, surpassing].
But I say that the bold transgressor will be brought down.
that can be transgressed or surpassed
that can be transgressed or surpassed
The great mind of Zeus is not to be transgressed, nor is it to be passed beyond.
I wet my cheek with watery streams.
I tear my tender cheek, warmed by the Nile.
The participle παρών [being present] is frequent, said of things that are present.
πάρεστι [it is present] means it is available, it is permitted, usually with an infinitive.
For πάρεστι [it is present] meaning it is at hand, πάρα [it is present] is used.
For πάρεστι [it is present] meaning it is available, it is permitted.
It is said equally of persons and things that are present, sometimes with a dative added, either of a person or of a thing.
